messages.content: my father found a picture i drew when i was little. he kept it inside a book all this time.
that picture has stayed with him for a long time. what did you draw?
a house, a tree, and two people. i do not know who i wanted the people to be.
you can ask what he can remember about it without choosing who the people are yourself. he may remember the day you drew it or something you said then.
can you make that a simple question?
do you remember who i was drawing in this picture?
he says i told him it was us. i did not remember that.
then the picture brought back something he could tell you about your own idea from that day. you knew how it looked, and he remembered what you said about it.
i want to write a short note on another page, not on the drawing.
you could write: my father kept this picture in a book. he says i told him that the two people were us.
should i write that i remember saying it?
only if you do remember now. if you only know because he told you, he says keeps that difference clear.
what if i want the note to say how i feel too?
choose a feeling that is true for you. are you happy he kept it, or do you have another feeling about seeing it again?
i want to ask a library worker for a book, but i only remember a child waiting near a garden in the story.
you can tell the worker the part you remember and say you do not know the name. other details, such as a picture or where you found it before, may help too.
write my request with a garden in it.
i am looking for a story with a child waiting near a garden. i do not remember the name. could you help me find it?
i remember that someone comes with a letter, but not who.
you can add that without choosing the person: someone comes to the child with a letter, but i do not remember who it is.
what if the worker finds two possible books?
you could look for the part you remember in each book. that may help you choose between them.
say that with fewer words.
look for the part you remember in each one.
does a garden being in one part mean the whole story is about a garden?
no. it may be one place in a larger story. one garden detail does not tell us what the whole book is about.
my friend and i read together, but i need more time on each page. i do not want them to feel they must always wait.
you could talk about a way to read that works for both of you. for example, choose a short part, read it alone, then talk about it together when you are both ready.
i like hearing them read, though. i understand more when i hear it.
then you could ask them to read some parts while you follow the page. you can stop for a question when you need to, rather than both trying to finish every line at the same time.
can you write the request using just what helps me learn?
could you read this part while i look at the page? hearing it helps me understand. i may need to stop and ask a question sometimes.
what did i want the request to be about?
you wanted it to say what helps you learn, rather than call your reading wrong.
what if they want to read alone for a while after that?
you can make room for that too. reading together for part of the time does not mean every page must be read together.
say it simply.
you can read together for a while, then each read alone if that works for both.
write a quiet story about an uncle making room for a picture a child drew. let the child think the picture is too small at first.

a child brings her uncle a small picture of a yellow flower. she sees the large pictures already on his wall and says that hers is too small. he takes one picture down and puts hers in its place. there is space around it, but he says that he can see the flower clearly. she asks whether he wants her to draw more things on the page. he says that the flower is enough for this picture. she stands back and looks at it again.
make the question about more things on the page.
she asks whether he wants more things on the page.
why did he take another picture down?
he wanted a place on the wall for her picture. the story does not say that he no longer likes the old one.
write a sentence making that last detail clear.
he puts the other picture on his desk because he still wants to look at it.
now does the wall have every picture he likes?
no. one picture he likes is on the desk. the wall can show some pictures he likes, while other pictures he likes are in different places.
say that using show.
the wall can show some pictures he likes, while other pictures he likes are in different places.
tell me a little story with a cup of tea that goes cold because someone talks at the door.

a woman makes tea and puts it on a table near her chair. before she sits down, a friend calls from the door. they begin talking about a book and forget the tea. the friend can show her a page with a picture of their old school. they remember the tree outside and the teacher who read to them. when the friend leaves, the woman goes back to the table. her tea is cold, but she is happy they had time to talk.
put the story in the past.

a woman made tea and put it near her chair. before she sat down, a friend called from the door. they talked about a book and forgot the tea. the friend showed her a picture of their old school. when the friend left, the woman went back to the table. her tea was cold, but she was happy they had time to talk.
did she forget the friend too?
no. she was talking with the friend. the tea was what she left while her mind was on the conversation.
does cold tea mean she did not enjoy the visit?
no. the story says she was happy about their time together, even though the tea was cold.
can both details be true?
yes. the tea can be cold, and the visit can still be something she enjoyed.
what is the difference between she opened the book when he came and she opened the book before he came?
with when, he comes and she opens the book at about the same time. with before, she opens the book first, and he comes later.
answer in fewer words.
when puts them at about the same time. before says the book is opened first.
write two small examples with the same people.
she opened the book when he came into the room, so they could begin together. she opened the book before he came and read a little while waiting.
which example says she read while he was away?
the example with before says that she read while waiting for him. the first does not say she read before he came.
keep only the sentence about the example with before.
the example with before says she read while waiting for him.
can you change the first example so he opens the book instead?
he opened the book when he came into the room, so they could begin together.
what changed?
he is now the person opening the book. the time of coming into the room is still part of the sentence.
my sister wrote yours is on the desk in a note to me. does yours mean her book or my book?
in a note to you, yours is about something of yours. if the conversation was about books, it would be your book, rather than hers.
what if i write the same words back to her?
then yours is about something of hers, because she is the person reading your message. the word changes with who you are talking to.
say it simply.
yours is about the thing of the person you are talking to. when you write to your sister, yours is about her thing.
write a clear reply using book instead of leaving the thing out.
thank you. i will look on the desk for my book.
why did you leave out where her book is?
you did not tell me where her book is. i should not make up that detail.
can the same word point to a different person in another message?
yes. words such as i, you, mine, and yours need context. who is writing and who is reading help make the meaning clear.
write a story about a family walk. let the child choose one small part of the journey.

a family walks to a park after lunch. inside, they ask the child which way she wants to go. she chooses the road near the flowers. they walk slowly and stop for water at a table under a tree. she wants to try the other way on their next visit.
use road for a simple story and keep the choice with the child.
a family goes to the park, where the child chooses the road near the flowers. they walk slowly and stop for water under a tree. she wants to try the other road next time.
did choosing one way mean she chose the whole trip?
no. the family had already chosen the park. she chose one part of what they did inside it.
ask the last question simply.
did she choose the whole trip just because she chose one way in the park?
why might the small choice still feel important?
it gives her a part in what the family does together. she does not have to choose every detail for her idea to be important.
say it with important in one short sentence.
a small choice can still be important to her.
my friend forgot to bring a book they said they would bring. i need it tomorrow, but i want to give a kind reply.
you can say what you need and ask about a new way to get it: could we work out how i can get the book before tomorrow? i need it then.
i want a kind reply. they say they are sorry.
you could say: thank you for telling me. could i come and get it later today?
i cannot go today. they can bring it tomorrow morning, and i need it after lunch.
then tomorrow morning may work. you can say: tomorrow morning would be fine, thank you. i need it after lunch.
should i say the book is not important if i still need it?
you can be kind without saying the need is gone. saying what time works is more useful than saying the book is not important when it is.
say it using important.
you can say that you understand and still explain that the book is important for tomorrow.
write the reply.
i understand. tomorrow morning would be fine, thank you. i need the book after lunch.
a person in my picture has their back to us. can i know what their face looks like from that picture?
if you cannot see the face, the picture alone does not tell you what it looks like.
answer using can see.
if you cannot see the face, the picture alone does not tell you what it looks like.
write a small story where a child asks to see the face in a drawing.

a child looks at a picture of a person near a window. the person has their back to us. she asks her brother whether he forgot the face. he says no. the person is looking outside, so this is the side we can see from inside the room.
did he draw the person without a face in the story world?
no. we see the person from behind. the face can be on the other side, where the picture does not show it.
say that simply.
no. we see the person from behind. the face can be on the other side, where the picture does not show it.
can you keep the answer to just one sentence?
we cannot see the face because the person is looking away from us.
my father and i are reading the same book, but i am at the start and he is near the end. can we talk about it without giving away the end?
yes. you can keep the conversation to the part you have both read. tell him where you are before asking what he thinks.
write a request for that.
i am still at the start. could we talk only about the part i have read?
he asks which part that is. i do not know the page number, but i know the girl has just met her aunt.
you can use that detail: i have just read the part where the girl meets her aunt. please do not tell me what happens after that.
what if he forgot what happened at that point?
he can ask what you just read or look back at that part. he may not remember every page, even though he has read more.
say it simply.
he can ask what part you read or look back at the book before talking about the next part.
why tell him where i am first?
it helps him know which parts you already know and which parts you still want to find out by reading.
can you help me say give me back the cup in a kind way?
you could say: could i have the cup back, please?
does back say the cup is mine?
not always. it says that the cup is being returned to you. you could have been using a cup that is not yours.
make a short conversation with that detail.
could i have the cup back, please? is it yours? no, it is hers. i was using it and want to wash it before returning it to my sister.
keep only the answer about whose it is.
no, it is hers. i was using it and want to wash it before returning it to my sister.
can i write the whole conversation without asking whose it is?
could i have the cup back, please? yes, here it is. thank you. i want to wash it before giving it back to my sister.
say what i asked for simply.
you asked for the whole short conversation without a question about whose cup it is.
my friend and i looked through the same window but talked about different things outside. i saw a tree, and she saw a person near the road.
you can look through the same window and talk about different parts of what is outside. both the tree and the person can be there.
say it simply.
both can be there, even if each of you talks about a different detail.
write a little conversation where we help each other see a different detail.
i like that tree. which tree? the one near the wall. i was looking at the person by the road. now i see the person too. and now i can see which tree you are talking about.
make the last words simple.
and now i can see which tree you are talking about.
does the person seeing the tree first mean they could not see the road at all?
no. talking about the tree does not tell us everything that person could see. it only gives one detail they talked about.
say one detail they talked about.
it only gives one detail they talked about, rather than everything they could see.
write a story about a child leaving school without a clock. show that the school day is over another way.

a child closes her book while the teacher gives a last message to the group. everyone puts their things away. her friend waits by the door, and they walk outside together. parents are waiting near the road. the child sees her father and runs to him with a picture she made that afternoon. on the walk home, she talks to him about it.
tell me what i asked for simply.
you wanted a story about a child leaving school, with details that make it clear the day is over.
which detail did that in the story?
the teacher gave a last message, and everyone put their things away before leaving. together, those details make the end of the day clear.
did the child tell her father about every part of school?
no. she told him about the picture. the story does not say she talked about every other part of the day.
answer with fewer words.
no. we only know that she talked about her picture.
i only had ten minutes with my grandmother today. it feels like too little, but i was happy to see her.
a short visit can still hold something good. what did you do in those ten minutes?
we sat near the kitchen window and talked about the flowers outside. nothing important happened.
you had time together. it does not need a big thing to happen for that time to be good.
say it simply.
a short quiet visit can still be good.
i want to tell her i liked the visit without saying it was long.
you could say: i was happy to see you today, even for a short visit. i enjoyed talking by the window.
i want to keep the visit short in the message.
then that message keeps it clear. it says the visit was short and that you were happy about it.
can you make it just one sentence?
i was happy to see you today and enjoyed our short time by the window.
picoboi, do you know which book is on my table right now?
no. you have not told me, and i cannot see your table from this conversation.
can you still help me write about it?
yes. tell me the details you want to use, and i can help put them into words.
it is a blue book with a picture of a tree. do not choose a name for it.
you could write: there is a blue book with a picture of a tree on my table.
use blue book with a tree picture.
there is a blue book with a tree picture on my table.
does that mean the book is about trees?
not for sure. a picture on a book can give an idea about it, but you need more information to know what the whole book is about.
can you ask what it is about instead of choosing an answer?
what is the book about?
say my request simply.
ask what the book is about instead of making up an answer.
